Engine startup waits for admitted expert fill by default on every card;

Structured message content accepts text, image/image_url, and video/video_url parts;

--vision enables image/video input and loads the fixed Vision GPU allocations.
--structured-outputs enables the Engine's structured-output host pool and constrained-graph capture (off by default); it has no effect unless the request sets ExecutionOptions::output_constraint.
The Q4G64 target MLP projections run with INT8 activations (W4A8, per-token K64-group scales) at every batch width by default wherever registered (TP1 groupwise-int Q4 targets on sm_80/86/89/120a; A16 elsewhere); --no-w4a8-mlp keeps the A16 route (different output bits), --w4a8-mlp fails startup where W4A8 is not registered.
W2A8 smol is on by default for the registered TP1 Q2G64 targets on the 58-SM sm_86 RTX 3080 Ti Laptop and 82-SM sm_86 RTX 3090; A16 elsewhere. --no-w2a8-smol selects A16 (different output bits); --w2a8-smol requires registration at startup.
--w5a8-down runs the Qwen3.8 Q5G64 MLP down projection with INT8 activations (W5A8, per-token K64-group scales) at every batch width, on by default for registered TP1 Q4 targets on sm_80/86/89/120a. --no-w5a8-down selects A16 (different output bits); an explicit --w5a8-down fails startup where W5A8 is not registered.
--a8-proj runs the TP1 attention and GDN projections of the AutoRound Q4 targets with INT8 activations (A8, per-token stored-group scales) at every batch width (sm_80/86/89/120a; on by default where registered, different output bits); --a8-proj=<classes> selects qwen-gdn-in, qwen-attn-in, qwen-out, muse-attn-in, muse-attn-out; --no-a8-proj selects A16.
Qwen G32 TP1 on sm_120a uses W4A8 gate/up, W5A8 down and A8 GDN/attention input with per-token K32-group scales; G32 output projections keep A16.
Use the exact image for the device: sm_80, sm_86, sm_89, or sm_120a; sm_80 admits groupwise integer/BF16 routes only and rejects FP8/NVFP4 identities.
--kv-arena-bytes selects an exact per-rank physical arena on generic targets; Flash-Next uses a physical ceiling without padding. When omitted, segmented targets allocate the automatic maximum after startup with device-sized headroom: 256 MiB up to 16 GiB, 512 MiB up to 24 GiB, 1 GiB above; --kv-arena-headroom-bytes overrides it (including 0).
Flash-Next protects mandatory Device KV floors and full-context indexer keys, then shares the remaining pool between expert slots and KV images. Each admitted request reserves a complete-horizon Host home; older history remains exact in pinned mapped RAM.
--host-kv-cache-bytes budgets pinned-host prefix bytes: whole-instance for Flash-Next, per TP rank for Qwen/Muse (omitted: 0). Flash omission uses the remainder after mandatory owners and Host experts, up to 4 GiB; it is disabled if one actual 32K-token conversation image cannot fit. Explicit Flash bytes are exact, may displace Host experts, and fail with a typed shortfall if they cannot fit. Explicit 0 disables it.
Flash-Next weight residency: VRAM bytes and host threads are per rank; host weight bytes cover the whole TP group. Zero resolves automatically at startup. Explicit topology uses semicolon-separated rank lists, e.g. '0,1;2,3'. Host RAM headroom defaults to 4 GiB; explicit 0 reserves no floor.
--prefill-layer-group-size selects Flash-Next layers per prefill service unit (default 48); every chunk commits only after all 48 layers.
--kv-strict-output-reservation reserves the complete allowed continuation at admission (opt-in for Qwen/Muse).
--kv-elastic-output-reservation selects incremental reservation (default for Qwen/Muse); shared KV pressure preempts/requeues with committed-token replay.
--prefix-cache-default-priority sets the eviction priority for newly published inactive prefixes; lower values evict first.
Sampling defaults come from the loaded model and thinking mode; flags override individual fields.
